HelloNation Article Featuring Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain Explains Dental Cleaning Frequency

HelloNation Article Featuring Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain Explains Dental Cleaning Frequency

PR Newswire

MOSES LAKE, Wash., Oct. 30, 2026

The article outlines how often patients should schedule cleanings to support gum health and long-term oral health maintenance.

MOSES LAKE, Wash., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How often should you get dental cleanings to maintain a healthy smile? The answer is explored in a HelloNation article featuring insights from Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain of Skyview Dental in Moses Lake, Washington.

The HelloNation article explains that dental cleaning frequency plays a central role in maintaining oral health. For many adults, visiting the dentist every six months is considered standard. This timing allows for consistent plaque and tartar removal before buildup can lead to more serious concerns. The article emphasizes that even with strong brushing and flossing habits, plaque can accumulate daily and eventually harden into tartar that requires professional dental cleanings.

According to the article, professional dental cleanings are designed to reach areas that routine home care may miss. These visits help reduce harmful bacteria and support long-term gum health. Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain is featured in the article, which highlights how regular Moses Lake dental cleaning appointments can make future visits easier and more comfortable by limiting buildup between appointments.

The article notes that while a six-month schedule works well for many, dental cleaning frequency varies for everyone. Some patients may benefit from more frequent visits, such as every three to four months. This is often recommended for individuals with a history of gum disease, heavy buildup, or health conditions that affect oral health. The article explains that personalized care plans help ensure effective gum disease prevention and better long-term outcomes.

Gum health is a key focus throughout the article. It describes how plaque and tartar removal helps prevent inflammation that can lead to gingivitis. If untreated, gingivitis may progress into more advanced gum disease, potentially affecting the bone that supports teeth. Regular professional dental cleanings reduce these risks and support healthier gums.

The HelloNation article also connects oral health maintenance with overall health. It explains that gum health has been linked to broader conditions such as heart disease and complications related to diabetes. By maintaining consistent dental cleanings in Moses Lake, patients can reduce inflammation and support both oral and general health.

Another important benefit discussed is early detection. The article explains how routine visits enable dental professionals to identify issues such as cavities and gum recession at an early stage. Addressing these concerns early often leads to simpler treatments and helps patients avoid more complex procedures later. Dental Expert Dr. Calvin Despain is included in the article as a source of insight on how consistent monitoring supports effective gum disease prevention.

The article further explains that maintaining a steady dental cleaning frequency improves patient comfort over time. With less plaque and tartar buildup, appointments tend to be quicker and more predictable. This consistency encourages patients to stay on track with their oral health maintenance routines and reinforces the importance of regular care.

For residents seeking guidance, the article emphasizes that the right schedule depends on individual needs. Factors such as medical history, lifestyle habits, and current gum condition all play a role. A personalized approach ensures that professional dental cleanings remain effective and aligned with each patient's oral health goals.

How Often Should You Get Dental Cleanings in Moses Lake? features insights from Dr. Calvin Despain, Dental Expert at Skyview Dental in Moses Lake, Washington, on HelloNation.

Through its community-focused publications and innovative "edvertising" approach, HelloNation delivers content that informs, inspires, and spotlights the leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities.

From Fairways to Futures: Swings for STEM Raises $100,000

From Fairways to Futures: Swings for STEM Raises $100,000

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Oct. 30, 2026

Third Annual Event Brings Together Chemical Industry Leaders, Policymakers, Academic Partners and Students to Strengthen Tomorrow's Workforce

WASHINGTON, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Alliance for Chemical Distribution (ACD) and American Chemistry Council (ACC) joined forces Monday for the third annual Swings for STEM golf tournament, raising $100,000 to support the next generation of scientists, engineers, and innovators. The event brought together stakeholders from industry, government and academia for a day of friendly competition and fundraising benefiting the Future of STEM Scholars Initiative (FOSSI) and Creating Exciting Futures in STEM (CEFinSTEM) , two organizations that seek to inspire, support, and expand access to STEM education.

"The future of our industry depends on the next generation of scientists, engineers, and innovators, and we have a responsibility to help them succeed," said Eric R. Byer, President and CEO of ACD. "Swings for STEM is about more than raising money. It's about opening doors, building relationships, and giving talented young people the opportunity to see what's possible in the chemical distribution industry. We're incredibly grateful to our sponsors, donors, and participants for helping us invest in the next generation of STEM leaders."

"Chemistry is at the heart of American innovation, and maintaining that leadership starts with investing in the next generation," added Chris Jahn, President and CEO of the American Chemistry Council. "When we launched FOSSI, our goal was to create new pathways into STEM careers and strengthen the chemical industry's talent pipeline. Today, more than 900 scholarships have been funded through that effort. Swings for STEM reflects that same vision, bringing industry and policy partners together to raise nearly $300,000 over the past three years."

The event also featured a dedicated student program for FOSSI scholars, combining a golf clinic, leadership development workshop, and networking opportunities.

FOSSI Scholar Brandon Simmons was one of nearly 20 scholarship recipients who attended the event, sharing, "My experience at Swings for STEM was truly rewarding. I enjoyed learning new techniques and connecting with fellow FOSSI scholars from different schools. The event was a great opportunity to build relationships, share experiences, and grow alongside other scholars. I'm grateful to FOSSI for creating opportunities like this that foster both personal growth and a strong sense of community."

To learn more about FOSSI visit www.FutureofSTEMScholars.org. Scholarship applications are open until January 8th, 2027. Eligible students can apply here.

To learn more about CEFinSTEM, visit www.cefinstem.org.

data.title: Is your crypto safe? What Binance's $6.3 billion hack means for bitcoin investors.
data.description:
By Isabel Wang and Joseph Adinolfi

A look at how safe your money really is when even the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange can be breached

Bitcoin and related stocks tumbled Friday after a record hack of the cryptocurrency platform Binance

A record $6.3 billion hack of Binance has put one of the crypto world's oldest risks back in the spotlight: How safe is investors' money when even the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange can be breached?

Prices of bitcoin and Ethereum were tumbling on Friday after Binance disclosed the hack - described as the largest relating to cryptocurrencies on record - that raises new concerns about whether investors can count on crypto exchanges to keep their assets safe.

Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was down 2.3% at $76,846 a coin in recent trading, while Ethereum (ETHUSD) was 1.2% lower, at $2,227, according to FactSet data.

Binance promised to cover all customer losses, and vowed to restart withdrawals within two days after freezing them as a security precaution. By working with industry partners, the exchange also managed to freeze about $3 billion in stolen assets, and the company has already started the recovery process, a Binance spokesperson told MarketWatch.

Nonetheless, the hack underscores a persistent challenge facing the cryptocurrency industry: convincing investors that their assets are safe in an ecosystem that continues to be plagued by security breaches.

"With certainty, we [investors] do have an inaccurate assessment of what occurred and the losses that happened in the market," said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and CEO at Global Settlement Network Institutional, a blockchain infrastructure firm. "Bitcoin is not recoverable."

In another statement to MarketWatch, Binance said it has already reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident, while $5 billion of these funds are already held in the exact token assets that were impacted. They are also completing the purchase of the remaining amount by buying token assets through market channels and over-the-counter channels, which may take longer, according to a Binance spokesperson.

Cybersecurity research firm TRM Labs said the attacker, which it identified as TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit, converted a large portion of the stolen funds into assets that are beyond any issuer's ability to claw them back.

In other words, promising depositors that "everything is under control" ignores the irreversible nature of blockchain transactions, Kirkley told MarketWatch via phone on Friday.

Putting money into the crypto market through an exchange is fundamentally different from investing in traditional, regulated markets, such as stocks and bonds. If your stockbroker goes bankrupt or fraud occurs, the Securities Investor Protection Corporation can protect your portfolio up to $500,000. However, crypto custodians, exchanges, brokers, wallet providers and neobanks often don't carry federal deposit insurance.

"Binance's ability to swallow what will be 5% of their entire holdings is remarkable, if they're able to do it, but to say they're able to do it without there being downstream sales and liquidations will be a very unlikely thing to happen," Kirkley added.

"We're talking about the world's largest crypto exchange relying on emergency freezes and reimbursement promises to contain a multibillion-dollar incident. That's a serious problem for an industry asking institutions to trust it with substantially more capital," Kirkley said.

The Binance hack isn't the only notable security incident to hit the crypto industry lately. Just last month, Bitget said that crypto worth roughly $350 million had been stolen from the platform, while a record $1.5 billion worth of Ethereum was stolen from the exchange Bybit early last year.

The onus is now on exchanges to prove customers' funds are secure. That's why until there is greater clarity around how this hack occurred, it is reasonable for investors to reassess how much capital they need to keep on the platform versus what can be held elsewhere, said Sean Farrell, head of digital asset strategy at Fundstrat.

Shares of crypto-related stocks were under pressure on Friday. Strategy (MSTR), Circle Internet Group (CRCL) and Coinbase (COIN) were all falling at least 9%, while shares of Robinhood (HOOD) were off nearly 10%, according to FactSet data.

Separately, Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform Thursday after hackers exploited an engineering flaw to drain between $2.5 million and $2.7 million from over 700 users' wallets. Polymarket has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of MarketWatch.

Hacks across the crypto industry have further dampened investor appetite for the once-popular risk asset. It has struggled in October after a late-summer rally brought bitcoin's price back above $70,000 for the first time in about three months. A number of other factors had been weighing on sentiment in the market, including expectations for more Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes in 2026, as well as fears that the voracious artificial-intelligence spending spree might not pay off.

Barbara Kollmeyer contributed

-Isabel Wang -Joseph Adinolfi

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal. 




  (END) Dow Jones Newswires

DOWNERS GROVE, Ill., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dover (NYSE: DOV), a diversified global manufacturer, today announced that it has amended its previously announced cash tender offers (the “Tender Offers”) to purchase the outstanding notes described below, by increasing the tender cap from an aggregate purchase price of $230,000,000 to $300,000,000 (the “Tender Cap”). Dover also announced that it will extend the Expiration Date of the Tender Offers. The Tender Offers are being made upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Offer to Purchase dated October 26, 2026 (the “Offer to Purchase”).

The Expiration Date for the Tender Offers has been extended to 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026, unless further extended or earlier terminated by Dover with respect to any Tender Offer. Tenders of Notes of a Series may be validly withdrawn at any time at or prior to 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026, but, except as provided in the Offer to Purchase or required by applicable law, may not be validly withdrawn thereafter. The Price Determination Date (as defined below) has correspondingly been extended to 3:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026.

The “Settlement Date” will be the second business day after the Expiration Date and is expected to be November 9, 2026.

The Notes offered to be purchased in the Tender Offers, in the order of acceptance priority, are the 6.650% Debentures due 2028; 6.600% Notes due 2038; 5.375% Debentures due 2035; and 5.375% Notes due 2041 (collectively, the “Notes”) for the consideration described below, up to the Tender Cap, subject to proration and the application of the Acceptance Priority Levels set forth in the table below and as further set forth in the Offer to Purchase. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this press release have the meanings given to them in the Offer to Purchase.

As of 12:30 p.m., New York City time, on October 30, 2026, approximately 28.86% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2028 Debentures, approximately 30.59% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2038 Notes, approximately 39.78% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2035 Debentures and approximately 30.83% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2041 Notes have been validly tendered in the applicable Tender Offers. In the event proration is required with respect to a Series of Notes, Dover will multiply the principal amount of each valid tender of such Series of Notes by the applicable proration rate and round the resulting amount down to the nearest integral multiple of the respective minimum denomination, in order to determine the principal amount of such tender that will be accepted pursuant to the applicable Tender Offer. The excess principal amount of Notes not accepted from the tendering Holders will be promptly returned to such Holders, and if this excess principal amount of Notes is less than the respective minimum denomination of such Series of Notes, Dover may either accept or reject all such tendering Holders’ validly tendered Notes in its sole discretion. Additionally, Dover may, but is under no obligation to, accept for purchase additional Notes of any Series in an aggregate principal amount not exceeding 2% of the outstanding aggregate principal amount of such Series without amending or extending the applicable Tender Offer, subject to applicable law, as further described in the Offer to Purchase, and may also further increase or decrease the percentage of the Notes accepted for payment in the Tender Offers (including by more than 2% of the outstanding aggregate principal amount of the Notes of the applicable Series) by a press release or other public announcement that is widely disseminated by no later than 9:00 a.m. (New York City time) on the third business day before the Expiration Date.

The “Total Consideration” for each Series of Notes payable per each $1,000 principal amount of such Series of Notes validly tendered for purchase will be based on the applicable Fixed Spread for such Series of Notes, plus the Reference Yield based on the bid-side price of the applicable Reference Security as quoted on the applicable Bloomberg Reference Page as of 3:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 5, 2026, unless further extended by Dover with respect to the applicable Tender Offer (such date and time with respect to a Tender Offer, as the same may be extended by Dover with respect to such Tender Offer, the “Price Determination Date”). Unless extended with respect to any Tender Offer, promptly after the Price Determination Date, Dover will announce in a press release, among other things, the Offer Yield and Total Consideration applicable to each Series of Notes accepted for purchase. In addition to the applicable Total Consideration, Holders whose Notes are accepted for purchase pursuant to a Tender Offer will receive accrued and unpaid interest on those Notes from the last interest payment date with respect to those Notes to, but excluding, the Settlement Date (the “Accrued Interest,” and the payment thereof, the “Accrued Coupon Payment”).

The Tender Offers are subject to certain conditions as described in the Offer to Purchase, including the Financing Condition, which requires that Dover shall have completed an offering (the “New Notes Offering”) of a new series of senior unsecured notes on terms and conditions satisfactory to Dover that results in its receipt of net proceeds that are sufficient to repay its €600,000,000 1.25% notes due 2026 at maturity. The New Notes Offering is expected to close on November 2, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

In no event will the information contained in this press release regarding the New Notes Offering constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any new notes. If any condition is not satisfied, Dover is not obligated to accept for payment, purchase or pay for, and may delay the acceptance for payment of, any tendered Notes, in each case subject to applicable law, and may terminate or alter any or all of the Tender Offers. The Tender Offers are not contingent upon the tender of any aggregate minimum principal amount of Notes of any Series (subject to minimum denomination requirements as set forth in the Offer to Purchase), and none of the Tender Offers is conditioned on the consummation of any of the other Tender Offers.

data.title: Insurance Expert Steven Barber Explains Hail Damage Insurance Claims for Homeowners in HelloNation
data.description:
Insurance Expert Steven Barber Explains Hail Damage Insurance Claims for Homeowners in HelloNation

Insurance Expert Steven Barber Explains Hail Damage Insurance Claims for Homeowners in HelloNation

PR Newswire

FORT WORTH, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026

The article explains how homeowners can document hail damage, review roof coverage, and understand insurance deductibles before filing a claim.

FORT WORTH, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Homeowners should check for visible hail damage from a safe location and document any signs of roof or property damage.
  • Reviewing homeowners' insurance can help homeowners understand roof coverage, deductibles, and how claim payments work.
  • Replacement cost coverage and actual cash value coverage can affect how much an insurance company pays for covered roof damage.

What should homeowners know before filing a hail damage insurance claim? A HelloNation article answers this question with insights from Steven Barber, Insurance Expert of Fort Worth, Texas. The feature explains how homeowners can identify storm damage, review their insurance policies, and prepare for the claims process.

How Should Homeowners Check for Hail Damage?

The article explains that hail damage is not always easy to see from the ground. Strong hail can crack shingles, loosen roofing materials, and leave dents in gutters. Some damage may also lead to leaks weeks or months after a storm.

Homeowners should begin by checking for visible damage from a safe location. Missing shingles, broken siding, and roofing materials on the lawn may point to storm damage. The article advises homeowners to avoid climbing onto their roofs and instead contact a qualified roofer for an inspection.

Steven Barber's insights also highlight the value of keeping clear records. Homeowners should take photos of visible damage, note the date of the storm, and save records of any repairs. These details may help support a roof insurance claim.

If water enters the home, homeowners should take reasonable steps to prevent further damage. Keeping receipts for temporary repairs may also be helpful because some homeowners insurance policies cover eligible costs to limit additional damage.

What Should Homeowners Review Before Filing an Insurance Claim?

The HelloNation article explains why reviewing homeowners insurance is an important step before filing a claim. Policy terms can affect what types of roof damage are covered and how much a homeowner may need to pay.

Most standard homeowners insurance policies provide some protection against sudden hail damage. However, coverage depends on the policy, the cause of the damage, and the roof's condition. Normal wear and poor upkeep are generally treated differently from damage caused by a recent storm.

An insurance deductible is another important factor. This is the amount a homeowner pays toward a covered loss before the insurance company pays its share.

For example, if covered roof repairs cost $8,000 and the deductible is $2,000, the insurer may pay $6,000, depending on the policy.

The article also explains that some policies have separate wind and hail deductibles. These may be set dollar amounts or percentages of the home's insured value. A two percent deductible on a home insured for $300,000 would equal $6,000.

Understanding these amounts can help homeowners estimate their costs before filing hail damage insurance claims.

How Does Roof Coverage Affect Insurance Payments?

The article identifies replacement cost coverage and actual cash value coverage as two important terms homeowners should understand.

Replacement cost coverage generally pays based on the cost of repairing or replacing covered damage with similar materials. Actual cash value coverage takes the roof's age and wear into account, which may lead to a smaller payment.

The article also explains that some replacement cost policies issue payments in stages. An insurance company may send an initial payment and release the remaining eligible amount after repairs are complete.

Homeowners may need to provide receipts or final repair documents before receiving the remaining funds. The exact process depends on the insurance policy.

Knowing how roof coverage works can help homeowners prepare for repair costs and understand what to expect during a claim.

What Happens After a Homeowner Files a Roof Insurance Claim?

According to the HelloNation article, homeowners who decide to file a claim should contact their insurance company and ask about the required documents and deadlines.

The insurance company may arrange an inspection to review the damage and determine what the policy covers.

Homeowners can also request a written repair estimate from a qualified roofer. Comparing that estimate with the insurer's findings may help identify differences in the proposed work.

The article notes that not every hail mark means a roof needs to be replaced. Homeowners should ask questions when repair recommendations or damage findings are unclear.

Keeping copies of photos, estimates, receipts, and claim messages can also make the process easier to follow. If an insurer denies part of a claim, homeowners can ask which policy terms apply and whether another review is available.

The article also encourages homeowners to be careful when hiring contractors after a major storm. Checking licenses where required, insurance, references, and written contracts can help homeowners avoid problems during repairs. Homeowners who are unsure which roofing company to hire can also contact their local insurance agent for a list of reliable roofing companies.

What Homeowners Should Know About Hail Damage and Roof Insurance Claims features insights from Steven Barber, Insurance Expert of Fort Worth, Texas, in HelloNation.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

What Should Homeowners Do First After a Hailstorm?

Steven Barber's insights in the HelloNation article explain that homeowners should check for visible damage from a safe location. Taking photos, recording the storm date, and arranging a professional roof inspection can help homeowners understand the damage before filing a claim.

Does Homeowners Insurance Cover Hail Damage to a Roof?

The article explains that most standard homeowners insurance policies cover some sudden hail damage. However, roof coverage depends on the policy terms, the cause of the damage, and the roof's condition. Normal wear and poor upkeep may not qualify for the same protection.

How Does an Insurance Deductible Affect a Hail Damage Claim?

According to the article featuring Steven Barber, an insurance deductible is the amount a homeowner pays toward a covered loss. Some policies have separate wind and hail deductibles that may be higher than the deductible for other claims.

What Is the Difference Between Replacement Cost Coverage and Actual Cash Value Coverage?

The HelloNation article explains that replacement cost coverage generally pays based on the cost of repairing or replacing covered damage with similar materials. Actual cash value coverage considers the roof's age and wear, which may reduce the claim payment.

How Can Homeowners Find a Reliable Roofing Contractor After a Hailstorm?

Steven Barber's featured insights encourage homeowners to check a roofing contractor's license where required, insurance, references, and written contract before agreeing to repairs. Homeowners can also contact their local insurance agent for a list of reliable roofing companies if they need help deciding whom to hire.

data.title: Insurance Expert Teri Cappadona Explains Texas Auto Insurance Requirements in HelloNation
data.description:
Insurance Expert Teri Cappadona Explains Texas Auto Insurance Requirements in HelloNation

Insurance Expert Teri Cappadona Explains Texas Auto Insurance Requirements in HelloNation

PR Newswire

BAYTOWN, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026

The article explains Texas minimum liability limits and what drivers should know about coverage after an accident.

BAYTOWN, Texas, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What are the minimum auto insurance requirements in Texas?A HelloNation article featuring insights from Teri Cappadona of Sapp Insurance Agency provides the answer.

The article explains that Texas drivers must be able to pay for accidents they cause. Most drivers meet this obligation through Texas auto liability insurance, which helps pay for injuries and property damage they cause to other people.

Texas auto insurance requirements establish minimum liability limits known as 30/60/25. These limits apply to each occurrence and represent the maximum amounts available for certain covered injuries and property damage.

The first number represents $30,000 in bodily injury liability for one person. This coverage can pay up to that amount toward covered costs, including medical bills and lost wages. The article notes that expenses from a serious injury can exceed this limit.

The second number represents $60,000 in bodily injury liability for one accident. This is the maximum amount the policy will pay toward the combined covered injury costs of everyone hurt in that accident, excluding the at-fault driver.

The article provides an example involving two injured people with $20,000 and $25,000 in covered costs. Their combined $45,000 in expenses falls below the $60,000 limit. A more serious crash involving emergency care, surgery, or extended treatment could exceed that limit.

The final number in 30/60/25 represents $25,000 in property damage liability for one accident. The article explains that this can apply to another person's vehicle or property such as a fence, garage, building, or utility pole.

These liability limits can become particularly important when newer or multiple vehicles are involved. Property damage can exceed $25,000, just as significant injuries can produce costs beyond the bodily injury limits.

The article also explains that Texas auto liability insurance generally follows the insured vehicle rather than the driver. When someone borrows a vehicle with the owner's permission, the owner's policy typically responds to a covered accident. However, if the driver is specifically excluded from the policy, coverage does not apply, potentially leaving both the driver and vehicle owner personally responsible for damages.

The article notes that the maximum amount an insurer will pay for a covered loss is determined by the limits shown on the policy's declarations page. When accident costs exceed those limits, the at-fault driver and vehicle owner, if they are different people, may be personally responsible for the remaining expenses.

The article explains that many drivers choose higher liability limits to help protect their savings, income, and property after a serious accident. Higher limits provide additional financial protection when covered claims exceed the state minimum. The appropriate amount depends on the assets and financial resources a driver wants to protect.

The article also clarifies an important limitation of Texas auto liability insurance. Liability insurance is primarily designed to pay for injuries and property damage a driver causes to other people. It does not automatically cover repairs to the driver's own vehicle.

Collision and comprehensive coverage serve different purposes. Collision coverage pays for covered repairs or replacement after a vehicle strikes another vehicle or object, regardless of fault, subject to the deductible on the declarations page. Comprehensive coverage, also called other than collision, addresses covered losses such as theft, vandalism, fire, windstorms, flooding, falling objects, or hitting an animal and is also subject to a deductible.

Neither collision nor comprehensive coverage is required under Texas law. A driver can meet the state's minimum liability requirements without carrying either coverage, potentially leaving their own vehicle unprotected after an accident or other loss.

The article concludes that Texas auto insurance requirements establish minimum liability limits that may not fully protect a driver's assets. When serious accident costs exceed those limits, the at-fault driver and vehicle owner, if they are different people, may face financial responsibility. Choosing higher liability limits can help protect savings, investments, and other assets from uncovered expenses.

Texas Minimum Auto Insurance Requirements: What the Liability Limits Mean features insights from Teri Cappadona, Insurance Expert of Baytown, Texas, in HelloNation.

data.title: ARC Awarded $10.9M Contract with Army DEVCOM Armaments Center to Advance Small Unit Resupply in Contested Environments
data.description:
ARC Awarded $10.9M Contract with Army DEVCOM Armaments Center to Advance Small Unit Resupply in Contested Environments

Armaments Research Company (ARC), Inc., a leader in advanced defense technology solutions, has been awarded a three-year, $10.9 million contract with the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC) through the Defense Ordnance Technology Consortium (DOTC) to continue its work transforming small unit resupply (SUR). Building on ARC’s prior SBIR Phase III task order with DEVCOM, this award advances the Army’s effort to solve the longstanding challenge of efficiently sustaining combat units at the front line in contested environments using autonomous platforms.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261029873012/en/

Over the three-year effort, ARC will further develop, integrate, and demonstrate its AI-enabled weapon sensors (AEWS) to operationalize SUR capabilities.

Over the three-year effort, ARC will further develop, integrate, and demonstrate its AI-enabled weapon sensors (AEWS) to operationalize SUR capabilities. The broader SUR architecture includes inventory management, and autonomous resupply platforms; connecting weapon data from the tactical edge with enterprise-level logistics and command-and-control integration systems. By capturing real-time weapon and ammunition data at the source, ARC’s sensors are being developed to enable predictive logistics, give commanders greater situational awareness of unit status, and support automated ammunition resupply so that distributed formations are resupplied at the time of need. ARC’s modular open system approach (MOSA) and technology platform is designed to adapt seamlessly as requirements and autonomous resupply platforms evolve.

“We’re proud to deepen our partnership with DEVCOM Armaments Center and continue building next-generation autonomous small unit resupply,” said Mike Canty, CEO of ARC. “Autonomy is changing how forces are sustained on the modern battlefield. This award pairs AEWS sensing with autonomy to increase warfighter survivability and lethality. We’re excited about the impact this capability can have across the force.”

This award reflects the Army’s continued commitment to rapid innovation and to collaborating with industry through flexible acquisition pathways like DOTC, accelerating the delivery of critical sustainment capabilities to America’s warfighters.

ABOUT ARMAMENTS RESEARCH COMPANY:

Armaments Research Company (ARC) is a technology company developing artificial intelligence-enabled weapons sensors for Enhanced Situational Awareness and Predictive Logistics in support of Large-Scale Combat Operations. Discover more at www.armaments.us.

data.title: Microsoft is winning the cloud wars and becoming Wall Street's new golden child
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone and Emily Bary

Various factors indicate that Microsoft is in a better financial position than its cloud rivals, analysts say

CEO Satya Nadella has won back Wall Street's trust.

After spending a good chunk of the past year in Wall Street's doghouse, Microsoft currently stands as the winner among the major cloud companies.

Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza issued that verdict following Amazon.com's (AMZN) Thursday earnings report, which showed cloud growth coming up short of what some investors were expecting.

Amazon's cloud business increased revenue at a 39% clip in the third quarter, while analysts tracked by FactSet had been expecting 37% growth. But institutional investors had been targeting growth more in the neighborhood of 43% to 44%, various analysts noted ahead of Amazon's report.

See also: Amazon's stock drops - even in the face of a bold new cloud forecast

The report from Amazon makes Microsoft (MSFT) "look even better," Favuzza wrote in a note to clients. That's even with the "frustrating price action" seen in Thursday's regular session, as Microsoft's stock gave back its early gains to close fractionally lower.

Microsoft's cloud growth seemed to sit better with Wall Street. The company increased revenue in its Azure cloud business by 48% in the September quarter, above a forecast for 44% to 45% growth that the company had offered back in September. And the company projected growth of 49% to 50% for the December quarter.

Favuzza wrote that the "tactical pecking order" among the big cloud companies seems to have Microsoft on top, followed by Meta Platforms (META), Amazon and then Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), which just saw its worst one-day stock decline on record.

Microsoft also stands out from the bunch because of its free cash flow, according to Greg Halter, the director of research at Carnegie Investment Counsel. The other three companies reported negative free cash flow for the third quarter, meaning that they spent more on infrastructure, data centers and related purchases than they generated in cash through their businesses. Microsoft's free cash flow stayed positive.

"We pay a lot of attention to FCF, and the market may be trying to instill some spending discipline into these companies," Halter said.

He hearkened back to the idea of "bond vigilantes," a famous term coined by economist Ed Yardeni to describe investors who shun debt until yields rise and they get paid more. Now, he noted, we might be looking at a case of "AI-spending vigilantes." Investors are drawing a hard line against companies deemed to be spending excessively without the returns to show for it.

Don't miss: Microsoft to raise up to $25 billion in bond market as investors get pickier about AI debt binge

Another thing working in Microsoft's favor is that the company "did more with less" - meaning that it was able to beat expectations with its Azure cloud growth even while capital expenditures, or infrastructure-related spending, came in $5 billion lower than the company had been modeling.

That's according to Patrick Walravens, the head of technology equity research at Citizens, who told MarketWatch that Microsoft's AI strategy is broadly resonating with customers.

"As AI advances faster and faster, the key thing enterprises are looking for is trust," he said. "Microsoft under [CEO Satya] Nadella's leadership has made trust a core part of its AI strategy, giving enterprises the ability to run, govern and distribute AI while retaining control of their data, models and intellectual property."

-Hannah Pedone -Emily Bary
